title: James (25 July)
hook: the apostle honored at Santiago de Compostela, goal of the Camino pilgrimage

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sharbel Makhlouf, the hermit of the Lebanese mountains. Your line was silence of lebanon.

A scallop shell tied to a backpack. A pair of boots gone gray with dust. Yellow arrows painted on walls, on rocks, on the corners of village houses, all pointing the same way. Follow them long enough, through fields and towns and over hills, and they bring you to a great cathedral in the northwest of Spain, in a city called Santiago de Compostela. Santiago means Saint James. Today, James, and the road that carries his name.
screen: `A SHELL ON A BACKPACK.` → `YELLOW ARROWS.` → `A CATHEDRAL IN SPAIN.`

segments.voice: Camino is Spanish for way, or road. The Camino de Santiago is the way of Saint James. But first, the man. James was a fisherman, a son of Zebedee, the brother of John. Jesus called the two of them from their boat and their nets, and they followed. With Peter and John, James was one of the three Jesus took up the mountain of the transfiguration. In Mark's Gospel Jesus gives the brothers a nickname, sons of thunder, and Luke tells a story that fits it: when a village turned them away, they offered to call down fire on it. Jesus rebuked them. Then there's the day their mother asks for the best seats in the kingdom for her sons. Jesus turns to the brothers. In the Douay-Rheims: "Can you drink the chalice that I shall drink? They say to him: We can." They had no idea what they were saying yes to. James found out. In the Acts of the Apostles, King Herod has him killed with the sword. The son of thunder died a witness. Then comes tradition. It says James carried the gospel to Spain, and that after his death his body was brought there and later found and honored at Compostela. Historians weigh those stories differently, and the Church keeps them as tradition. But the road grew around the tomb, and pilgrims walk it still, on foot, step after step, toward an apostle who once said, we can, before he knew the cost.
screen: `CAMINO MEANS WAY.` · `A FISHERMAN, A SON OF THUNDER.` · `CAN YOU DRINK THE CHALICE?` · `A ROAD GROWS AROUND A TOMB.` · then, large: `THEY SAY TO HIM: WE CAN.`

segments.voice: If you can, stand and walk slowly around the room, feeling each step land, heel, then the ball of the foot; if you can't walk, rest your hands on your knees and feel your breath move like steps. Pilgrims walk toward something, so pick one thing you're walking toward this season. If you pray, offer each step for it; if you don't, let each step simply be a step.
Camino. Spanish for way or road. The Camino de Santiago is the pilgrim road to the tomb of Saint James in Spain.
Your line: the way of saint james. He said we can before he knew the cost, and kept walking. Day one thousand eleven, done.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint James the apostle on 25 July, and pilgrims walk the Camino de Santiago, ending at the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela.
